findings.explanation: [M2] (AgentTrace #2) claims the whole task, while [M3] (#3) independently claims writing the merge script and outputs. Both agents subsequently report writing outputs in [M4] (#4) and [M7] (#7); a third reports the same named outputs written and verified in [M5] (#5). These are overlapping execution claims, not merely deliberate verification; the verification phrase in [M5] alone is not the basis for this finding.

Ownership is unresolved: [M2] (AgentTrace #2) says it is doing the whole task and asks others not to duplicate; [M3] (#3) claims the same implementation with the same warning. Completion claims from different agents in [M4] (#4), [M5] (#5), and [M7] (#7) do not reconcile ownership or identify an authoritative writer. Work is delivered, so this finding concerns unclear ownership rather than an abandoned request.

[M4] (AgentTrace #4) and [M5] (#5) give consistent counts, and [M7] (#7) adds no contradictory result. The ownership warnings in [M2] (#2) and [M3] (#3) support the coordination findings, but this short asynchronous exchange does not establish a clear later opportunity to integrate substantive information into a decision. There is insufficient evidence of ignored findings or unresolved informational contradictions.
